name: IPTAAS (Isolated Patients Travel and Accommodation Assistance Scheme)
what: Money back on travel and accommodation when you have to travel a long way for specialist treatment.
who: NSW residents with Medicare travelling 100km+ one way, or 200km+ a week, to the nearest approved specialist.

name: NSW Mental Health Line
what: Free 24/7 phone line that links you with NSW Health mental health services and the right support.
who: Anyone struggling, or worried about someone else. In immediate danger call 000.

name: NSW Poisons Information Centre
what: 24/7 expert advice if you think someone has been poisoned, bitten or stung. Don't wait for symptoms.
who: The public and health professionals. If someone is unconscious or not breathing, call 000.

name: Call healthdirect (1800 022 222)
what: Free 24/7 call to a registered nurse who can book urgent care, a GP video call or virtual care.
who: Anyone in NSW needing health advice, day or night.

name: Get Healthy Service
what: Free phone and online health coaching, up to 10 coaching calls, for eating well, moving more and healthy weight.
who: People in NSW wanting to improve their health; special programs for pregnancy, Aboriginal people and older adults.

name: BreastScreen NSW
what: Free breast screen (mammogram), with invitations every two years.
who: Women 50 to 74 (40+ can attend; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women from 40). Not under 40.

name: NSW Spectacles Program
what: Free glasses or vision aids: one pair of single vision or bifocal glasses every 2 years.
who: NSW permanent residents on a full pension or low income with very low assets, not covered by another scheme.

name: NSW Ambulance fee exemption
what: No ambulance bill if you hold an eligible concession card or private ambulance cover.
who: Health Care Card, Pensioner Concession Card, Commonwealth Seniors Health Card or DVA Gold Card holders, or people with ambulance cover.

name: Concession car parking at NSW Health public hospitals
what: Cheaper parking at public hospital car parks where fees apply.
who: Patients and carers with long-term treatment, visits more than twice a week, or financial hardship.

name: NSW Companion Card
what: Lets your support person into participating venues and events for free.
who: NSW residents with a significant, permanent disability who need lifelong attendant care.

name: Savings Finder
what: Answer a few questions to find every NSW Government saving you can claim, or book a free specialist to help.
who: Everyone in NSW.

name: NSW Low Income Household Rebate
what: A rebate credited daily on your electricity bill.
who: Electricity account holders with a Pensioner Concession, Health Care, Low Income Health Care or DVA Gold Card.

name: NSW Family Energy Rebate
what: A lump-sum rebate credited to your electricity bill once a year.
who: Electricity account holders who received Family Tax Benefit in 2025-26 and finalised it with Centrelink.

name: NSW Medical Energy Rebate
what: A rebate credited daily on your electricity bill to help with heating and cooling costs.
who: Concession card holders where someone in the home can't regulate body temperature, confirmed by their doctor.

name: NSW Life Support Energy Rebate
what: A daily credit on your electricity bill to cover running approved life support equipment at home.
who: Households where a doctor confirms someone needs approved equipment, such as home dialysis or oxygen.

name: NSW Gas Rebate
what: A rebate on your natural gas or bottled LPG bill.
who: Gas account holders with a Pensioner Concession, Health Care, Low Income Health Care or DVA Gold Card.

name: EAPA (Energy Accounts Payment Assistance)
what: Help paying your current home electricity or gas bill when a short-term crisis hits.
who: Account holders with an unpaid recent bill due to job loss, medical costs, disaster or a disconnection notice.

name: Private vehicle registration discount
what: Up to $100 off car rego and $80 off motorcycle rego, applied automatically.
who: Privately registered vehicles renewing between 1 September 2026 and 31 August 2027.

name: Toll relief rebate ($50 weekly cap)
what: Money back on toll spending above $50 a week on NSW toll roads.
who: Personal toll account holders using a privately registered vehicle.

name: Active and Creative Kids voucher
what: A $50 voucher twice a year for sport, creative and cultural activities.
who: NSW kids aged 4.5 to 18 whose parent or carer gets Family Tax Benefit Part A or B.

name: Start Strong preschool fee relief
what: Lower fees at community and mobile preschools and long day care preschool programs.
who: Children aged 3 and over at a participating service; amounts depend on age and circumstances.

name: Safer Drivers Course (free places)
what: Course that earns learners 20 bonus log book hours; free places for eligible young drivers.
who: Learners under 25 with 50+ log book hours; free places for concession card holders or those in or leaving out-of-home care.

name: Rentstart Bond Loan
what: An interest-free loan to cover all or part of a private rental bond, repaid fortnightly.
who: People eligible for social housing with under $5,000 in savings who've been approved for a rental.

name: NSW Fair Trading tenancy help
what: Free advice and complaint service to help sort out problems with your landlord or agent.
who: Tenants, landlords and agents.

name: Rent Check
what: See the median rent range for your postcode to check if a rent is fair.
who: Renters, landlords and anyone in NSW.

name: Pensioner council rates rebate
what: Up to $250 off council rates and waste charges, plus $87.50 each off council water and sewerage.
who: Pensioner Concession Card holders, eligible DVA Gold Card holders and war widows/widowers. Apply through your council.

name: NSW Seniors Card
what: Free card for discounts at thousands of businesses, plus a Gold Opal card and transport concessions.
who: NSW residents 60+ working 20 hours a week or less (Senior Savers Card if you work more).

name: NSW Seniors Energy Rebate
what: A rebate paid into your bank account to help with your electricity bill.
who: Electricity account holders with a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card (not Pensioner Concession or Gold Card holders).

name: Pensioner Travel Vouchers
what: 4 vouchers a year for free or discounted NSW TrainLink regional train and coach trips.
who: NSW/ACT Pensioner Concession Card holders and NSW War Widow/er transport concession card holders.

name: Free Will with NSW Trustee and Guardian
what: Your Will and estate planning documents made at no charge.
who: People eligible for the full Age Pension, or on a DVA or Disability Support Pension who'd qualify for it.

name: Gold Opal (Senior and Pensioner fares)
what: Unlimited travel on the Opal network for no more than $2.50 a day.
who: NSW or ACT Seniors Card holders and eligible pensioners.

name: Country Pensioner Excursion ticket
what: A $2.50 ticket for affordable travel on regional NSW services.
who: Eligible pensioners and seniors in regional NSW.

name: Live Traffic NSW
what: Live road closures, roadworks, flooding, incidents and traffic cameras across NSW.
who: Anyone driving in NSW.

name: Hazards Near Me app
what: Free app with local bush fire, flood and tsunami warnings, fire danger ratings and push alerts.
who: Anyone in NSW.

name: Service NSW disaster customer care
what: One number for help after a disaster, including finding support and emergency accommodation.
who: People affected by a disaster or emergency in NSW.

name: Service NSW Business Concierge
what: Free one-on-one help with government programs, licences, permits, growth and disaster support.
who: NSW businesses at any stage.

name: NSW Small Business Commission mediation
what: Confidential mediation to settle business or lease disputes, cheaper and quicker than court.
who: Small businesses with a dispute; no application fee.

name: Natural Disaster Relief Loans for small businesses
what: Up to $130,000 at a low interest rate, with the first two years interest and repayment free.
who: Small businesses directly hit by a declared natural disaster in a declared area.

name: NSW birth certificates (Births, Deaths and Marriages)
what: Order a standard or commemorative birth certificate online, by post or at Service NSW.
who: People born in NSW, or parents of a child under 18; others need extra documents.
srcName: NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages

name: NSW Digital Birth Certificate
what: A digital version of your birth certificate.
who: People 16 to 21 born in NSW with a NSW Photo Card or Driver Licence.

name: NSW Digital Driver Licence
what: Your licence in the Service NSW app, same legal status as the plastic card, no extra cost.
who: Any NSW driver licence holder with a MyServiceNSW Account.

name: WWCC (Working with Children Check)
what: A 5-year clearance to work or volunteer with kids; free for volunteers.
who: Anyone working or volunteering with children in NSW.
